executive_summary: The Docker environment hosting the ICS lab has critical security risks due to a vulnerable 'router' container with excessive capabilities and network exposure. The container's image contains 5 critical CVEs (3 fixable, 2 unpatched) and bridges multiple networks (admin, ICS, DMZ), creating a high-risk attack surface. Privileged network capabilities (CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_NET_RAW) could allow an attacker to manipulate ICS network traffic or escalate privileges.

findings.title: Critical Image Vulnerabilities in Router Container
findings.explanation: The router container's image has 5 critical vulnerabilities, including unpatched issues in zlib1g and libsqlite3-0. In an ICS context, exploitation could allow network manipulation or container escape, directly impacting process control systems.
findings.remediation: Update the 'router' image to patched versions (perl-base 5.36.0-7+deb12u4) and replace vulnerable components (zlib1g, libsqlite3-0). Isolate the container from the ICS network using network policies.

findings.title: Excessive Network Capabilities in Router Container
findings.explanation: CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_NET_RAW allow full network control. If exploited, an attacker could modify firewall rules, intercept traffic, or disrupt ICS communications.
findings.remediation: Remove CapAdd directives from the container configuration. Use network policies instead of capabilities for required functionality.

findings.title: Multi-Network Bridging in Router Container

findings.explanation: The container bridges admin, ICS, and DMZ networks. A compromise could allow lateral movement from the DMZ to the ICS network, bypassing network segmentation controls.
findings.remediation: Restrict the container to a single network (preferably admin) and use dedicated network appliances for ICS-DMZ routing.

findings.title: Unrestricted Port Exposure in Router Container
findings.explanation: Port 51820/UDP is exposed to all interfaces. In an ICS environment, this increases the attack surface for tunneling or man-in-the-middle attacks.
findings.remediation: Restrict port binding to specific internal IPs using HostIp parameter. Implement network ACLs to limit access to trusted sources.

recommendations: Immediately update the 'router' container image to address critical CVEs (especially perl-base 5.36.0-7+deb12u4)
Remove CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_NET_RAW capabilities from all containers
Implement network segmentation using Docker networks and firewalls to isolate ICS components
Conduct regular vulnerability scans using Trivy with minSeverity=HIGH
Replace the 'router' container with a hardened, minimal image if vulnerabilities remain unpatched
limitations: Cannot verify runtime exploitation of vulnerabilities
Cannot assess network traffic patterns or firewall rules
Cannot check if other containers have similar misconfigurations (only 'router' was fully analyzed)
